title: An overview of Zombie.js and HTML Unit

videos.script: Every tool so far in this course has driven a real browser: Chromium, started by Playwright, Selenium or Puppeteer. This lesson is about the other kind. {{pipeline}} A simulated browser is a program that reads the HTML, builds the tree of elements, and runs the page's scripts. It never draws anything. There is no layout, no paint and no screen. {{zombie}} Zombie.js was the well-known one in Node. Its last release came out in 2018, and you will see what that means for a page written today. {{htmlunit}} HtmlUnit is the Java one, and it is still released. You point it at the shop and watch its JavaScript engine refuse the shop's script. {{jsdom}} Then you run jsdom, the library behind Jest's jsdom environment. It loads the shop, draws the eight cards, and puts a banana in the basket. {{misses}} Next you ask it what lesson seven asked Chromium. How wide is the page? It answers zero, and the check for a page that scrolls sideways passes on a page that is broken. {{fit}} Last, you time both kinds against each other, and decide where a simulated browser earns its place. Fast checks of HTML, and unit tests of code that touches the page.
